Solar Energy Systems Engineer said about it: For this device power sizing follows the array formula in How to Size an Off-Grid Solar System (5-Step Guide) | Off Grid Collective USA (E3), which divides daily load by worst-month Peak Sun Hours (PSH, equivalent hours at 1000 watt per square metre) and by 0.75 system efficiency, with hot-region resource of about 5.0 PSH from Insolation in Solar: Meaning and Why It Matters (E7) and 400 watt modules from Spectra 400W 48V Rigid Solar Panel - Monocrystalline PERC (E9); then the array sizing estimate (E13) gives 2.13 kilowatt for 8.00 kilowatt-hour per day, the daily yield estimate (E14) gives 9.00 kilowatt-hour per day from 2.40 kilowatt peak, and the night autonomy simulation (E15) shows about 13.3 kilowatt-hour per day load is not covered so about 3.50 kilowatt peak is needed, which is about one household daily use and therefore an everyday scale.
